get.description: Report that the process is up. Reads no configuration and no database.

post.description: Accept one file, extract its text, and store it as the single active resume.

413.description: The upload is larger than the configured limit

415.description: The declared type, or the bytes, are not a readable resume

422.description: The upload is corrupt, carries no text, or is not a named file part

get.description:
Every company on the watchlist, in ascending id order, active or not.

No filter and no paging: one user's watchlist is short, and an inactive
company is still a company to show.

post.description:
Add one company, once its board has answered and only if its slug is new.

The board is asked before anything is written, and every `POST` asks it once:
a body that cannot be used never reaches this function, and a slug that is
already watched is refused only after the source has spoken for it.

404.description: No board goes by that slug, or no company has that id

409.description: The slug is already on the watchlist

422.description: The body, or the path, is not something this route can use

502.description: The board could not be read: it is down, slow or malformed

delete.description:
Delete exactly that company, and answer `204` with no body when it went.

The id is a path parameter and an `int`: a value that is not one never
reaches this function and is refused by the path's own validation as `422`.
An id that finds no row is a `404` and deletes nothing.

404.description: No board goes by that slug, or no company has that id

422.description: The body, or the path, is not something this route can use

post.description:
Start one run, and answer `202` with the row this request wrote.

The caller is checked first, then the guard is claimed, then the row is
written, then the work is handed over -- and the answer carries that row in
status `running` rather than waiting for the work, which is what
`GET /runs/{id}` is for. Nothing before the hand-over can leave the guard
held: a row that cannot be written, like work that cannot be started, is a
`500` and gives the guard back, so the endpoint recovers instead of refusing
every later tick.

202.description: A run started: the run row this request wrote

401.description: The request's shared internal header is missing, empty or wrong

409.description: A run is already in progress in this process

500.description: The run could not be recorded, or its work could not be started

get.description:
The run with that id, in whichever status it is in, exactly as the row holds it.

The id is a path parameter and an `int`: a value that is not one never
reaches this function and is refused by the path's own validation as `422`.
An id that finds no row is a `404` and invents nothing.

422.description: The path value is not a run id

get.description:
Every `match` row, newest first, and `[]` when there are none.

No filter, no search and no paging: `_docs/plan.md` asks only that the UI
browse matches, and one user's matches are few. The order is `created_at`
descending with the id descending under it, so two rows written in the same
instant -- which `created_at`'s default makes possible -- still have one
order, newest row first.

patch.summary: Record the owner's verdict on one match
patch.description:
Write the owner's `saved` or `dismissed` verdict on that match, and answer with it.

The id is a path parameter and an `int`: a value that is not one never
reaches this function and is refused by the path's own validation as `422`.
A body whose `state` is neither of the two verdicts is refused by
`MatchVerdict` the same way. An id that finds no row is a `404` and writes
nothing. What is written is `state` and nothing else, and the answer is the
row as `GET /matches` renders it, read after the write -- so the same verdict
sent twice is the same answer twice and one row the whole time.

422.description: The body, or the path, is not something this route can use

file.title: File
file.description: A PDF, a DOCX or a UTF-8 text file

CompanyCreate.title: CompanyCreate
CompanyCreate.description:
Body of an addition: the name to show, and the board slug to poll.

Both fields are required strings, and a string that carries nothing but
whitespace is refused as well: the name labels a row a person reads, and the
slug is what the source is asked about. The values are left exactly as they
were sent; normalising the slug is `app.models.Company`'s, not this model's.

MatchSummary.title: MatchSummary
MatchSummary.description:
One `match` row as this API renders it: the row, plus the names it points at.

The same body both routes carry, so a client reads one shape for a match
wherever it meets one. Nine fields and no tenth: `notified_at` stays on the
row, because when an alert went out is the digest's business and not the
screen's, and nothing here is computed -- `score`, `reason` and `state` are
the row's own, `gaps` is the list #8 stored as JSON text, and `id` is what
`PATCH /matches/{id}` takes.

MatchVerdict.title: MatchVerdict
MatchVerdict.description:
Body of a verdict: the one value this endpoint records, and no other field.

`state` is a `Literal` of the two verdicts the owner has, so anything else --
`"new"`, `""`, a number, nothing at all -- is refused by this model's own
validation as `422` and never reaches the row. Re-opening a match as `new` is
not in `_docs/plan.md`, and the column's own vocabulary is the model's
(`ck_match_state_values`) rather than this endpoint's.

ResumeUploaded.title: ResumeUploaded
ResumeUploaded.description: Body of a successful upload: which resume is now the active one.

RunSummary.title: RunSummary
RunSummary.description:
One `run` row as this API renders it: its seven columns, and no derived field.

The same body a `202` from `POST /internal/tick` carries. `finished_at` and
`error` are absent until the run ends, and both counts are 0 from the moment
the row is written: what the boards returned and how many matches
`record_score` wrote (#34), never a score computed here.

WatchedCompany.title: WatchedCompany
WatchedCompany.description:
One watchlist entry as this API renders it: four fields, and no timestamp.

The same body `POST` answers with, so a client reads one shape for a company
wherever it sees one. `created_at` is stored and not exposed.
